name: Rhind papyrus worked mathematical text
summary: An Egyptian papyrus copied by the scribe Ahmose, holding worked problems in arithmetic, fractions and areas, one of the oldest surviving mathematics texts.
description: The mathematical text preserved in the Rhind papyrus: worked problems with arithmetic, fractions and areas, copied by the scribe Aḥmose.
tier_reason: Retain2 for the papyrus witness. Its status as chief surviving witness is not enough to promote it under the owner's consequence test. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

impact.note: A problem text of Egyptian scribal practice, copied from an older one; it served one society's administrators and its methods persisted in a few later texts.

market.note: This node is scoped to mathematical knowledge and scholarly interpretation.

date.label: About 1650–1550 BCE (different scholarly estimates)
date.basis: Chace’s 1927 edition estimates about 1650 BCE; the modern British Museum exhibition guide estimates about 1550 BCE. These two approximate estimates define the displayed range, not proven chronological limits.

events.statement: Aḥmose copied a mathematical text that includes arithmetic and geometric problems.
events.caveats: The British Museum estimates about 1550 BCE, while Chace’s older edition gives about 1650 BCE; the competing estimates and approximate range do not establish an exact copying year. The particular copied exemplar is lost; the scribe’s understanding and contemporary readership are not demonstrated.
